name: Bahrain

fees.name: Tourist eVisa (2 weeks, single entry)
fees.applies: eligible nationalities (nationals of ~212 countries eligible online)
fees.notes: Split payment on evisa.gov.bh: BD 4 non-refundable application fee paid first, BD 9 visa fee paid on approval (total BD 13). Proof of funds required (bank statement, ~BD 300-500/month income).

fees.name: Multiple-entry visitor eVisa (1 year)
fees.validity: 1 year, multiple entry (up to 90 days per stay)
fees.notes: Requires hotel reservation, return ticket, and bank statement.

fees.name: Multi-entry return visa (5 years)
fees.applies: nationals of UK, Ireland, Canada, USA
fees.notes: Available only to UK, Irish, Canadian and US nationals.

fees.name: Family visit eVisa
fees.applies: applicants with kinship to a resident/citizen sponsor
fees.notes: Requires kinship documentation, hotel reservation, return ticket, bank statement.

fees.name: Visa on arrival (2 weeks)
fees.applies: eligible nationalities (~69 countries, list on evisa.gov.bh)
fees.notes: BD 25 is widely published by airline/visa-industry sources for the 2-week VOA at Bahrain International Airport; exact amount could not be confirmed on the fee page of evisa.gov.bh (portal blocks automated access, fees shown at payment step). Eligibility list itself is official.

fees.name: Visit eVisa extension (2 weeks, single entry)
fees.applies: holders of an existing visit visa

fees.name: Business visit visa
fees.notes: Business visits are generally covered by the same eVisa/visit-visa fee schedule or NPRA sponsored visas; no separate published business-visa fee was verifiable on official sources.

fees.name: Transit
fees.notes: No separate published transit-visa fee found on official sources; airside transit without entering Bahrain requires no visa. Travellers entering during layovers use the eVisa/VOA.

reciprocity_variations.note: Eligible for the special 5-year multi-entry return visa (BD 50) in addition to standard eVisa options (also Ireland).
eVisa-eligible online; standard fee (BD 4 application + BD 9 visa). Indians with valid US/UK/Schengen visas or GCC residence are also VOA-eligible.
Generally not eligible for unsponsored eVisa/VOA; require a sponsored NPRA visit visa. Fee depends on visa type granted; not published as a flat schedule.

free_visa_notes: GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) nationals do not require a visa to enter Bahrain. All other nationalities need an eVisa, visa on arrival, or sponsored visa.
